re_line: Xi state visit in Washington, $30 billion tariff relief, Taiwan arms package on hold, Perdue arms-sale remark, China aid to Iran
editors_note: Xi's Washington visit produced $30 billion in reciprocal tariff relief, a November AI dialogue and a coal pledge, but left export controls, AI governance and Taiwan unresolved. A $14 billion Taiwan arms package remains on hold.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Fuel export approvals unclear as Golden Week ends Oct. 7
week_at_a_glance.body: Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and PetroChina cancelled a small number of planned gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on Sept. 30, Reuters reported.
week_at_a_glance.why: Lianhe Zaobao said it is unclear whether Beijing will resume approvals after the holiday ends Oct. 7.

week_at_a_glance.headline: PBOC reverse repo of 1.2 trillion yuan set for Oct. 8
week_at_a_glance.body: The PBOC will run a 1.2 trillion yuan three-month buyout reverse repo operation on Oct. 8, part of a package that includes a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy effective Oct. 1, Reuters reported.
week_at_a_glance.why: Bloomberg cited analysts saying the package is likely to secure Beijing's GDP target for the year but deliver little additional lift.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Golden Week travel heads to Southeast Asia, not Japan
week_at_a_glance.body: China's seven-day holiday began Oct. 1 with over 2 billion passenger trips expected, many headed to Southeast Asia rather than Japan, Nikkei Asia reported.
week_at_a_glance.why: Japan's tourism agency data showed Chinese visitors fell roughly 60 percent year-on-year in August amid bilateral tensions.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Wicker says U.S. must honor Taiwan commitments
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker said Washington's security commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taiwan's Representative to the U.S. Alexander Yui, the Taipei Times reported.
heard_on_the_hill.why: Four other Republican senators separately called on the Trump administration to release more than $14 billion in stalled Taiwan security assistance.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson rejects arms package as trade leverage
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Speaker Mike Johnson said Taiwan's stability is important to U.S. national security and dismissed suggestions that a delayed $14 billion arms package is being used as leverage in trade talks, the Taipei Times reported.
heard_on_the_hill.why: He said Trump will have completed roughly $40 billion in Taiwan arms sales across two terms.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate bill would bar Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan Senate group proposed legislation banning Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period, Jiemian reported.
heard_on_the_hill.why: Chinese optical and communications stocks sold off Sept. 28, with ChiNext down 4.53 percent and the SSE Composite down 3.2 percent to a one-year low.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate delays Chinese car ban until after midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate punted a bill that would permanently ban Chinese-made cars from the U.S. market until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, AP reported.
heard_on_the_hill.why: Reuters reported senators plan to bring the measure up again for a vote in November.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Moreno says his vehicle bill spares Mercedes-Benz
heard_on_the_hill.body: Sen. Moreno said a bill he is sponsoring to bar companies with more than 15 percent Chinese ownership from selling vehicles in the U.S. would not affect Mercedes-Benz, CNBC reported.
heard_on_the_hill.why: The bill targets Chinese-linked automakers amid a broader congressional push on connected-vehicle restrictions.

in_the_news.headline: China, US agree $30 billion reciprocal tariff cut, new AI dialogue after Xi's Washington visit
in_the_news.body: Reuters reported China's foreign ministry said the Sept. 23-25 Xi-Trump summit produced an eight-point consensus, including $30 billion in reciprocal tariff relief and a new AI dialogue with the next round set for November, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the tariff truce was extended by two months, per the Financial Times. The tariff lists published Sept. 28 cover roughly $60 billion of two-way trade but leave off soybeans, Reuters reported, and CNN, citing Nikkei, said rare earths stayed off both lists.

in_the_news.headline: Xi presses Trump to 'oppose' Taiwan independence
in_the_news.body: Xi Jinping pressed Donald Trump to 'oppose' Taiwan independence at their Sept. 24 White House meeting, Bloomberg reported, and Taiwan's government accused Xi of 'distorting facts,' per Reuters. A $14 billion Taiwan arms package remains stalled, AP reported, while Trump said only that Xi 'knows how I feel' on the issue.

in_the_news.headline: Chinese intelligence aids Iran's improved targeting of US forces
in_the_news.body: Satellite imagery and intelligence support from Chinese groups has helped Iran strike U.S. military bases with improved precision, according to U.S. intelligence assessments described to CNN by four sources. Reuters reported that Ambassador David Perdue said Trump warned Xi at the summit that Chinese assistance to Iran was "totally unacceptable" and received assurances.

in_the_news.headline: Trump denies offering to sell US arms to Xi after ambassador says he did
in_the_news.body: Trump said he had "never heard of" offering to sell weapons to Xi, contradicting Ambassador David Perdue's claim on Fox News that Trump made the offer at the summit, AP reported. The State Department said the U.S. has no plans to sell weapons to China, the Wall Street Journal reported, and the Guardian cited PBS reporting that Trump later said Perdue 'was probably talking about Taiwan.'

in_the_news.headline: US Officials See Chinese Invasion of Taiwan Unlikely Before 2028
in_the_news.body: U.S. officials believe Beijing is unlikely to use force against Taiwan before 2028, even though Xi has ordered the PLA to be ready by 2027, Reuters reported, citing two current U.S. officials, a former official and another source. Officials pointed to an anti-corruption purge that leaves only two of seven Central Military Commission members in active service, including Xi.

research_roundup.headline: Trump rolled out the red carpet – and handed Xi a narrative win
research_roundup.body: A Lowy Institute piece argues Trump handed Xi a narrative win, with China's deference to history and protocol masking "a calculated bid for narrative dominance."

research_roundup.headline: How Beijing could throttle Taiwan without firing a shot
research_roundup.body: A Lowy Institute piece on how Beijing could throttle Taiwan without firing a shot argues that administrative quarantine "sounds anodyne" but for Taiwan "is war by other means."

research_roundup.headline: A paradoxical purge: Xi shows his power, and his trouble in controlling the PLA
research_roundup.body: ASPI argues Xi's continuing purge of senior PLA leadership reveals both the reach of the Chinese Communist Party's disciplinary apparatus and the persistence of disloyalty.

research_roundup.headline: The PRC’s Compute Push Goes Global
research_roundup.body: The Jamestown Foundation finds Chinese firms "languishing under a compute crunch" from U.S. export controls on high-end GPUs, with Huawei, Cambricon and Biren Technologies yet to fill the gap, and argues the PRC's compute push has gone global anyway.

research_roundup.headline: Revolting for the CCP: seizing Taiwan could drive Japan to nuclear weapons
research_roundup.body: ASPI argues potential Japanese acquisition of nuclear weapons is an under-appreciated deterrent to a Chinese attempt to seize Taiwan.
